title: Back to Sleep: In Peace I Will Lie Down

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
You are awake in the night. That is all right. [pause 10]

Leave the lights off. Let the phone lie face down beside you. [pause 12]

Here is one short line from Psalm 4, read twice, very slowly. [pause 12]

verses.text: I will both lay me down in peace, and sleep: for thou, LORD, only makest me dwell in safety.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
Lay me down in peace. That is all there is to do right now. Lie down. [pause 15]

Nothing has to be solved at this hour. It will keep until morning. [pause 15]

Two more short lines for the night. [pause 12]

verses.text: When I remember thee upon my bed, and meditate on thee in the night watches.
I laid me down and slept; I awaked; for the LORD sustained me.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
David remembered God on his bed, in the night watches. You can do the same, without any words. [pause 15]

And he lay down, and slept, and woke again. The Lord held him through the night. [pause 15]

Here is the line from Psalm 4 once more. [pause 15]

verses.text: I will both lay me down in peace, and sleep: for thou, LORD, only makest me dwell in safety.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
Now let it be quiet. [pause 12]

Let your breathing slow down on its own. In, and out. [pause 15]

Nothing is needed from you. He does not sleep, so you can let go. [pause 20]

Rest. [pause 60]

first_reader.note: Drafted and read by Claude in the landing session; no free-model draft (QA_NO_FREE_MODEL not needed).

pastor.note: Grief nights and the 3 AM night (21 Nov 2026): every passage is stored KJV pasted by code (Ps 13, Ps 23, John 11:32-36, Ps 4:8 and companions); written lines echo in short phrases only. Lament is allowed (How long) without rebuke; no reason given for a death, no 'better place', no timeline for grief (the grief_words check); Rev 21:4 told as the hope at the end of the story, not a claim about the person who died; Jesus's and God's words given indirectly outside scripture. Each grief night points to a pastor or a grief counselor; the 3 AM night makes no sleep promise.

cultural.note: Plain, unhurried English a grieving or half-awake listener can follow at 3 AM; the person who died is 'them', never assumed to be a spouse, parent or child; no pity, no hurry ('nobody is timing you'); the 3 AM night is short and spare, the phone face down. Lengths by silence only: grief nights 10-11.5 min, the 3 AM night 6 min (estimated at 117 wpm).
